### LOW: Dev\-branch signing/publish run can now be cancelled mid\-flight by a later dispatch
[\.github/workflows/release\-dev\-branch\.yml:49](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/08e8af1f35cf01b4fde29506834665d91154161e/.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml#L49) · new attack surface

The dev lane previously used \`cancel\-in\-progress: false\` with the note that a running run always completes\. The head sets \`cancel\-in\-progress: true\` on group \`release\-dev\-branch\-dev\`\. The called release\-provider\.yml runs inside this caller's concurrency scope, so a second \`workflow\_dispatch\` on \`dev\` cancels the whole in\-flight run, including Developer ID signing, notarization, R2 staging and registration\. Registration or staging can then be left half\-finished, and each new run gets a new run\_number version\. Any repository writer can dispatch \(no inputs, \`github\.ref == refs/heads/dev\` is the only check\) and can keep cancelling releases, or leave staged but unregistered artifacts\. This replaces the push trigger, which only ledger\-bypass accounts could fire\. Fix: keep \`cancel\-in\-progress: false\` for the \`dev\` group, or cancel only before the signing and publish jobs\. Restrict dispatch to authorized actors\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Label\-only trigger can turn the threat\-review clearance gate into a skipped \(passing\) check on new pushes
[\.github/workflows/threat\-model\-review\.yml:71](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/08e8af1f35cf01b4fde29506834665d91154161e/.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml#L71) · new attack surface

The review job now runs only when the \`run\-threat\-model\` label is added \(\`types: \[labeled\]\`, \`if: \.\.\. github\.event\.label\.name == 'run\-threat\-model'\`\)\. The old trigger covered opened/synchronize/reopened/edited, and the removed comment explained that in clearance mode an edited PR must not replace a failed required run with a skipped success\. The workflow still supports \`THREAT\_REVIEW\_REQUIRE\_CLEARANCE=true\` \(continue\-on\-error, membership token and the \`threat\-review\-gate\.py after\` step\), so that mode remains in use\. If it is enabled and the job is a required check, any push without a fresh label produces no run, or a skipped job that GitHub counts as satisfied\. A later push to the head SHA can therefore merge without a new review or clearance evaluation, bypassing the review of provider/attestation\-affecting code\. Whether the gate is required is repo configuration not supplied here\. Fix: in clearance mode, keep the synchronize/reopened triggers, or add an always\-running gate job that fails unless a review or override exists for the current head SHA\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Clearance mode: unrelated label now yields a skipped \(passing\) job in place of a clearance run
[\.github/workflows/threat\-model\-review\.yml:71](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/08e8af1f35cf01b4fde29506834665d91154161e/.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml#L71) · new attack surface

The old \`if\` carried a comment that, in clearance mode, an edited PR must not replace a failed required run with a skipped success\. The new \`if\` \(line 71\) only runs the job when the label is \`run\-threat\-model\`, and the trigger is now \`types: \[labeled\]\` \(line 6\)\. With THREAT\_REVIEW\_REQUIRE\_CLEARANCE=true, any other label event on a new head SHA makes the \`review\` job skip, and GitHub treats a skipped job as a passing required check\. A user with triage rights \(or automation\) could add an unrelated label after a push or a failed run, so a required threat\-model check could show as skipped/green with no \`threat\-review\-gate\.py after\` evaluation\. Fix: when clearance is required, keep the job running for every event and fail or pend closed unless the run\-threat\-model label is present, or run the gate in a separate job that always executes\. Whether this applies depends on how the required\-check rule is configured, which is not visible here\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The concurrency group is now `release-dev-branch-dev` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (was `false`). A later manual `workflow_dispatch` on `dev` cancels the entire running caller workflow, including the reusable chain's `build-and-release`, `stage-release` and `publish-release` jobs. The inner `provider-publication-dev` group is `cancel-in-progress: false`, but it does not stop the outer cancellation. Trigger: a second dispatch while a run is notarizing, staging to R2 or registering with the dev coordinator. Impact: orphaned staged R2 objects or a partly registered release in the dev release and binary-hash registry. The file's own re-run note says a repeated signing attempt is refused with HTTP 409. Fix: keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for the build group, or cancel only while the run is before signing, and leave publication uncancelled.
findings.title: Workflow-level cancel-in-progress can kill an in-flight dev release during signing, staging or registration

findings.detail: The patch changes runs-on for stage-release (base line 1210) and publish-release (base line 1319, head 1320) from blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 to ubuntu-24.04, and the same swap applies to resolve-env and a qualification job. Those jobs resolve and use R2 write credentials and the coordinator RELEASE_KEY (A-005), then register hashes in the provider binary hash registry (A-011). The workflow's own comment says to "keep the older-OS proof within the release trust boundary", so runner placement is treated as a boundary. The jobs still take secrets only after hash-pinned tool installation and use pinned actions, so no concrete exploit is shown. The runner trust and isolation change is undocumented and the threat model does not say which runner pools may hold release credentials. Fix: record in the threat model or workflow that GitHub-hosted runners are accepted for these jobs, or keep them on the prior pool.
findings.title: Release publication jobs holding R2 and release-key secrets moved from Blacksmith to GitHub-hosted runners

findings.detail: Head line 71 gates the `review` job on `github.event.label.name == 'run-threat-model'`, while the workflow still fires on every `labeled` event (line 6). Any other label added to a PR creates a run in which the `review` job is skipped. A skipped job reports as a passing check on that head SHA. The base workflow had a comment (base lines 70-71) saying clearance mode must not let a skipped success replace a failed required run. When `THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE=='true'`, a triager or any label-capable actor who adds an unrelated label (e.g. `bug`) after a failed or incomplete review can leave a skipped, green check on the same SHA. That would bypass the `threat-review-gate.py after` evaluation. The base `edited`-event carve-out was dropped without a clearance-mode equivalent. Fix: run the job in clearance mode regardless of label, or add a lightweight job that fails or stays pending until the gate has evaluated the head SHA. Alternatively, trigger only through a dedicated label-filtered mechanism that does not emit a required-check conclusion for other labels.
findings.title: Label-gated threat review job skips on unrelated labels, which can satisfy a required clearance check

findings.detail: For a one-parent (squash) push, candidates() now adds a ("tree", None, None, ...) candidate. With record_head=None, tested_run() accepts any successful run of the same workflow file whose head_sha is merely a valid 40-hex SHA, from pull_request or push, whose artifact is named ci-tested-tree-<tree>-<flags>. Previously a record had to match the exact PR head, or the merge commit's actual parents. A same-repo PR runs its own, possibly modified, workflow, so a branch writer can make that workflow upload an empty ci-tested-tree-<T>-p1c1m1 artifact for a predicted tree T and finish green without running tests. If T later lands by squash merge (for example another PR's reviewed content on the current base), the push run skips its tests on the strength of that forged record. The docstring at lines 33-35 says the tree hash makes the record trustworthy, but the artifact name is not bound to what the producing run tested. Fix: require the producing run's head tree to equal T, or have the producer's own commit/tree checked via the API. Alternatively, restrict tree records to push runs of protected branches.
findings.title: Tree-keyed CI records drop the head/base binding, so a same-repo PR run can vouch for another change's tree

findings.detail: threat-model-review.yml still fires on every `labeled` event, but the `review` job is gated on `github.event.label.name == 'run-threat-model'` (head line ~71). Adding any other label creates a run in which `review` is skipped, and a skipped job reports as passing for that head SHA. The base workflow had a comment that clearance mode must not let a skipped success replace a failed required run. The `edited` carve-out was removed with no clearance-mode equivalent. findings.detail: For a one-parent (squash) push, candidates() adds a ("tree", None, None, ...) candidate. With record_head=None, tested_run() accepts any successful run of the same workflow file, from a pull_request or push, whose artifact is named ci-tested-tree-<tree>-<flags>. Previously a record had to match the exact PR head or the merge commit's real parents. A same-repo PR runs its own, possibly modified, workflow. A branch writer could make it upload an empty ci-tested-tree-<T>-... artifact for a predicted tree T and finish green without running tests. If T later lands by squash merge, the master push run skips its tests on the strength of that forged record. Fix: bind the record to what the producing run actually tested, for example by checking the producing run's head tree against T. Alternatively, accept tree records only from push runs on protected branches.
findings.title: Tree-keyed CI records drop the head/base binding, so a same-repo PR run can vouch for another change's tree

findings.detail:
In head scripts/ci-tested-tree.py:144-146, a tree record (record_head is None) passes `head_ok` for any run whose head_sha is a well-formed SHA. Lines 122 and 124 also accept the record from either `pull_request` or `push` events. The base design bound each record to its own change by requiring head_sha == record_head. That binding is why the base docstring (line 31-32) said a record of one change could not stand in for another.

The artifact name is chosen by whatever workflow content ran. A same-repository PR can edit its own copy of the workflow (the docstring at lines 33-34 admits records are only as trustworthy as the workflow at that head). Such a PR could upload `ci-tested-tree-<T>-p1c1m1` for an arbitrary future tree T without running tests. Path equality (line 148) does not check workflow content. When a later squash or merge push to master produces tree T (lines 121-124), it skips every test.

Before this change, a forged record could only match a push whose parents were that PR's own base and head.

Fix options:
- Bind tree records to a run whose head commit's tree equals T. For example, fetch `git/commits/<run.head_sha>` and compare the tree, or use the PR merge-commit tree.
- Alternatively, accept tree records only from push runs on protected branches.
findings.title: Tree-only CI records accept any same-workflow run regardless of head, so a forged record can skip tests for an unrelated change

findings.detail:
Record flags (head ci-tested-tree.py:83-84, 91-92) encode only provider, cluster and mimo_audio, not cluster_gpu. The updated test at scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py hunk @@ -377 shows how the GPU lane is gated:
- A pull_request without the run-gpu-ci label runs cluster with cluster_gpu=false.
- A master push with skip=false runs cluster_gpu=true.
- A master push with skip=true runs cluster_gpu=false.

With the new tree candidate (ci-tested-tree.py:122-124), a run-ci-labeled PR into master can upload a c1 tree record without any GPU testing. A squash merge that yields the same tree then matches that record and skips the master push, so the GPU cluster lane never runs on the release line.

Fix: include cluster_gpu in record flags, or refuse tree records from runs that did not run the GPU lane when the current run would.
findings.title: Tree record reuse lets a master push skip GPU cluster tests that it would otherwise run
